finding.claim: deleteAccount ignores the boolean returned by canDelete, so the authorization check is never enforced. Any caller can delete any account by id.
finding.source: Authenticated user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id (no ownership required)

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) handles DELETE /accounts/{id}; id is from the URL
Account loaded by request id with no owner check
canDelete(u,a) result is discarded; no if/throw

finding.guards_checked: canDelete at line 9-11 is correct but its return value is unused. closeAccount uses assertCanDelete, which throws, so it is fine. No other middleware exists in the repo, which has a single file. A null account (unknown id) would NPE in canDelete, but that does not stop deletion of valid ids.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (lines 9-11) returns a bool, but its result is discarded at line 22. assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) throws, but it is only used by closeAccount (line 29). No other controls exist in the single-file repo.
verdict.reason: src/AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete(u,a) as a bare statement and discards the result, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user and any existing id, which makes this a broken-authorization flaw.
